lines.text: **Section 4.01 Organization and Qualification**

The Company is a corporation duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Oregon. The Company has full corporate power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and assets and to carry on its business as currently conducted. The Company is duly qualified or licensed to do business and is in good standing in each jurisdiction where the character of its properties owned or leased or the nature of its business makes such qualification or licensing necessary, including the States of Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. Seller has made available to Buyer true, correct, and complete copies of the articles of incorporation and bylaws of the Company, as currently in effect.
**Section 4.02 Authority**

The Company has full corporate power and authority to execute and deliver this Agreement to the extent it is a party hereto and to perform its obligations hereunder. The execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement by the Company (to the extent it is a party hereto) have been duly and validly authorized by all necessary corporate action on the part of the Company.
**Section 4.03 Capitalization**

The authorized capital stock of the Company consists of 5,000,000 shares of common stock, par value \$0.01 per share, of which 1,000,000 shares are issued and outstanding as of the date hereof. All of the issued and outstanding shares of common stock of the Company have been duly authorized, are validly issued, fully paid, and nonassessable, and were issued in compliance with all applicable Laws and in accordance with the Company\'s articles of incorporation and bylaws. There are no outstanding options, warrants, convertible or exchangeable securities, subscriptions, rights (including preemptive rights or rights of first refusal), stock appreciation rights, phantom stock, profit participation, calls, commitments, or agreements of any kind relating to the capital stock of the Company, or obligating the Company to issue, deliver, sell, repurchase, or redeem any shares of its capital stock. There are no outstanding or authorized equity-based awards, stock appreciation rights, phantom stock awards, profit interests, or similar rights with respect to the Company. There are no outstanding agreements, contracts, or commitments restricting the transfer of, or requiring the registration for sale of, any shares of the capital stock of the Company. There are no anti-dilution or similar adjustments with respect to any equity securities of the Company.
**Section 4.04 Subsidiaries**

The Company does not own, directly or indirectly, any equity interest, capital stock, membership interest, partnership interest, joint venture interest, or other ownership interest in any other Person. The Company has no subsidiaries.
**Section 4.05 No Conflicts; Consents**

The execution, delivery, and performance by the Company of this Agreement (to the extent it is a party hereto), and the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, do not and will not (a) conflict with or violate the articles of incorporation or bylaws (or other organizational documents) of the Company, (b) conflict with or violate any Law or order applicable to the Company or by which any property or asset of the Company is bound or affected, or (c) result in any breach of or constitute a default (or an event that, with the giving of notice or lapse of time, or both, would become a default) under, give rise to a right of termination, cancellation, modification, or acceleration of, or result in the creation of any Encumbrance upon any of the properties or assets of the Company under, any contract, agreement, instrument, Permit, or other arrangement to which the Company is a party or by which the Company or any of its properties or assets is bound or affected, except, in each case of clauses (b) and (c), where such conflict, violation, breach, or default would not, individually or in the aggregate, be material to the Company. Schedule 4.05 sets forth a true and complete list of all consents, waivers, approvals, authorizations, and notices required to be obtained or made in connection with the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement and the consummation of the transactions contemplated hereby.
**Section 4.06 Financial Statements**

Seller has delivered to Buyer (a) the audited balance sheets of the Company as of December 31, 2022, December 31, 2023, and December 31, 2024, and the related audited statements of income, stockholders\' equity, and cash flows for each of the fiscal years then ended, together with the reports thereon of Winslow & Tate CPA Group, independent certified public accountants, and (b) the unaudited balance sheet of the Company as of September 30, 2025, and the related unaudited statements of income and cash flows for the nine-month period then ended (the financial statements described in clauses (a) and (b) above, collectively, the \"Financial Statements\"). The Financial Statements have been prepared in accordance with GAAP applied on a consistent basis throughout the periods covered thereby and present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of the dates thereof and the results of operations and cash flows of the Company for the periods indicated therein, subject, in the case of the unaudited interim Financial Statements, to normal year-end adjustments (which are not expected to be material in the aggregate) and the absence of footnotes. The books and records of the Company have been maintained in all material respects in accordance with GAAP and applicable Laws.
**Section 4.07 No Undisclosed Liabilities**

The Company does not have any liabilities, obligations, or commitments of a type that would be required to be reflected on a balance sheet prepared in accordance with GAAP, except (a) liabilities reflected or reserved against in the Financial Statements, (b) liabilities incurred since September 30, 2025 in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice (none of which results from, arises out of, relates to, or was caused by any breach of contract, breach of warranty, tort, infringement, or violation of Law), (c) liabilities arising under the executory portions of contracts to which the Company is a party (not resulting from any breach or default by the Company), (d) Transaction Expenses, and (e) liabilities set forth on Schedule 4.07.
**Section 4.08 Absence of Changes**

Since September 30, 2025 through the date of this Agreement, (a) the Company has conducted its business in the ordinary course of business consistent with past practice in all material respects, and (b) no event, change, effect, development, condition, or occurrence has occurred that has had or would reasonably be expected to have, individually or in the aggregate, a Material Adverse Effect.
**Section 4.09 Real Property**
**(a)** The Company does not own, and has never owned, any real property.

**(b)** Schedule 4.09 sets forth a true and complete list of all real property leased, subleased, or licensed by the Company (the \"Leased Real Property\"), including the address, landlord, annual rent, lease term, and renewal options with respect to each such lease. The Company has a valid and enforceable leasehold interest in each parcel of Leased Real Property, free and clear of all Encumbrances (other than Permitted Encumbrances). The Leased Real Property constitutes all of the real property used or occupied by the Company in the conduct of its business. The Company has made available to Buyer true, correct, and complete copies of all leases, subleases, and other occupancy agreements (including all amendments, modifications, supplements, side letters, and guarantees) relating to the Leased Real Property. Each such lease is in full force and effect and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, of the other parties thereto. Neither the Company nor, to the Knowledge of the Company, any other party thereto, is in breach or default (or has received written notice of a breach or default) under any such lease. The Leased Real Property includes a facility leased from Parkside Realty Holdings LLC, an Affiliate of Seller, at an annual rental of \$1,600,000 (the \"Affiliate Lease\"), as further described on Schedule 4.09.
**Section 4.10 Personal Property**

The Company has good and valid title to, or a valid and enforceable leasehold interest in, all tangible personal property and assets used in the conduct of its business as currently conducted, free and clear of all Encumbrances other than Permitted Encumbrances. Such personal property is in good operating condition and repair (subject to normal wear and tear) and is adequate and suitable for the purposes for which it is presently being used. The equipment financing with Pacific Lease Corp. in the amount of \$9,800,000, relating to specified environmental remediation equipment and vehicles, is disclosed as a Permitted Encumbrance.
**Section 4.11 Intellectual Property**

**(a)** *Registered Intellectual Property.* Schedule 4.11(a) sets forth a true and complete list of all registered trademarks, service marks, copyrights, and patents and all pending applications therefor owned by the Company, including the registration or application number, the jurisdiction of registration or application, and the current status thereof.

**(b)** *Proprietary Software.* Schedule 4.11(b) describes the proprietary software applications owned by the Company, including the remediation tracking software known as \"GreenSite,\" which is maintained as a trade secret and has not been registered with the United States Copyright Office. The Company has taken commercially reasonable steps to protect the confidentiality and proprietary nature of the GreenSite software and related source code.

**(c)** *Third-Party Licenses.* Schedule 4.11(c) sets forth a true and complete list of all material licenses, sublicenses, and other agreements pursuant to which the Company is authorized to use any intellectual property of a third party (other than commercially available, off-the-shelf software licensed on standard terms with annual license fees of less than \$50,000). Each such license is in full force and effect and constitutes a valid and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, of the other parties thereto. Neither the Company nor, to the Knowledge of the Company, any other party thereto, is in material breach or default under any such license.

**(d)** *No Infringement.* To the Knowledge of the Company, the conduct of the Company\'s business as currently conducted does not infringe upon, misappropriate, or otherwise violate the intellectual property rights of any third party. There are no Actions pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened against the Company alleging any such infringement, misappropriation, or violation. To the Knowledge of the Company, no third party is infringing upon, misappropriating, or otherwise violating the intellectual property rights of the Company.
**(e)** *Sufficiency.* The Company owns or has a valid right to use all intellectual property that is material to the conduct of the Company\'s business as currently conducted.
**Section 4.12 Tax Matters**

**(a)** The Company has timely filed (taking into account any valid extensions of time for filing) all Tax Returns required to be filed by it. All such Tax Returns are true, correct, and complete in all material respects.

**(b)** The Company has timely paid all Taxes required to be paid by it (whether or not reflected on any Tax Return), and has withheld and remitted to the appropriate Governmental Authority all Taxes required to be withheld and remitted by it.

**(c)** There are no Actions pending or threatened in writing against the Company with respect to any Taxes. There are no outstanding written assessments, deficiencies, or proposed adjustments of any Tax with respect to the Company. No audit, examination, or other administrative or judicial proceeding relating to Taxes of the Company is currently in progress or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened.

**(d)** The Company has not waived any statute of limitations in respect of Taxes or agreed to any extension of time with respect to a Tax assessment or deficiency, which waiver or extension remains in effect.
**(e)** There are no Encumbrances for Taxes upon any of the assets of the Company (other than Permitted Encumbrances for Taxes not yet due and payable).

**(f)** The Company is not a party to, bound by, or obligated under any Tax-sharing, Tax-allocation, or Tax-indemnity agreement or arrangement (other than any agreement entered into in the ordinary course of business the primary purpose of which is not the allocation or payment of Taxes, and other than any agreement with Seller as part of Seller\'s affiliated consolidated group for federal income Tax purposes, which agreement shall be terminated on or prior to the Closing Date).

**(g)** The Company has been included in the affiliated consolidated group (within the meaning of Section 1504 of the Code) of which Seller is the common parent for federal income Tax purposes. The Company is not, and has not been, a member of any other affiliated group, consolidated group, combined group, or unitary group for Tax purposes.
**(h)** The Company has not been a party to any \"reportable transaction\" within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.6011-4(b).
**Section 4.13 Material Contracts**

**(a)** For purposes of this Agreement, \"Company Material Contracts\" means any contract, agreement, instrument, arrangement, or commitment (whether written or oral) to which the Company is a party or by which the Company or any of its properties or assets is bound that:
> \(i\) involves the payment or receipt of amounts in excess of \$500,000 per year;

> \(ii\) is an employment, consulting, severance, change-of-control, retention, or similar agreement with any employee, officer, director, or independent contractor of the Company with annual compensation in excess of \$150,000;
> \(iii\) is a contract with any Governmental Authority;
> \(iv\) is a contract with Seller or any Affiliate of Seller;
> \(v\) contains any non-competition, non-solicitation, exclusivity, most-favored-nation, or similar restrictive covenant;
> \(vi\) involves the licensing of intellectual property (other than commercially available, off-the-shelf software);
> \(vii\) is an equipment lease, capital lease, or financing arrangement;
> \(viii\) relates to Indebtedness; or
> \(ix\) is otherwise material to the business, operations, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company.

**(b)** Schedule 4.13 sets forth a true and complete list of all Company Material Contracts, including, without limitation: (i) the government contracts with Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, Washington Department of Ecology, United States Army Corps of Engineers, and Bureau of Land Management; (ii) the employment agreements with Patricia Huang, Brian Kowalski, Sandra Firth, and David Alarcon; (iii) the Affiliate Lease with Parkside Realty Holdings LLC (\$1,600,000 annual rent); (iv) the subordinated seller note payable to Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc. (\$4,500,000); (v) the TerraSpatial Inc. GIS mapping software license (\$180,000 per year); (vi) the senior term loan agreement with Cascade Mutual Bank (\$28,000,000); (vii) the equipment financing facility with Pacific Lease Corp. (\$9,800,000); and (viii) the environmental liability insurance policies with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co.

**(c)** Seller has made available to Buyer true, correct, and complete copies of all Company Material Contracts (including all amendments, modifications, supplements, and side letters thereto). Each Company Material Contract is in full force and effect, is a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, of the other parties thereto, and is enforceable in accordance with its terms. Neither the Company nor, to the Knowledge of the Company, any other party thereto, is in material breach or default under any Company Material Contract, and no event has occurred that, with the giving of notice or the lapse of time, or both, would constitute a material breach or default thereunder.
**Section 4.14 Employees and Employee Benefits**

**(a)** *Employees.* As of the date hereof, the Company employs approximately 340 full-time employees and no part-time employees. The Company is not a party to, nor is it bound by, any collective bargaining agreement or other contract or arrangement with any labor union or labor organization. There are no pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened labor disputes, work stoppages, slowdowns, lockouts, picketing, or strikes, and no union organizing campaigns are pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened with respect to the employees of the Company. The Company is and has been in compliance in all material respects with all applicable Laws relating to labor and employment, including Laws relating to wages, hours, overtime, classification of employees and independent contractors, immigration, equal employment opportunity, non-discrimination, sexual harassment, occupational health and safety, workers\' compensation, and the Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (and any comparable state or local Laws).

**(b)** *Employee Benefit Plans.* Schedule 4.14(a) sets forth a true and complete list of all Employee Benefit Plans. The Company does not sponsor, maintain, or contribute to any \"defined benefit plan\" (as defined in Section 3(35) of ERISA) or any \"multiemployer plan\" (as defined in Section 3(37) of ERISA). The Employee Benefit Plans include a 401(k) defined contribution plan with a four percent (4%) employer matching contribution. Each Employee Benefit Plan has been established, maintained, funded, and administered in compliance in all material respects with its terms and with all applicable Laws, including ERISA and the Code.

**(c)** *Professional Licenses.* Schedule 4.14(b) sets forth a true and complete list of the twelve (12) employees of the Company who hold professional engineer (\"PE\") licenses, including the name, license number, and state of licensure of each such employee. To the Knowledge of the Company, all such PE licenses are in good standing and no Action is pending or threatened to revoke, suspend, or limit any such license.

**(d)** *Key Employees.* The key employees of the Company include Patricia Huang (Chief Executive Officer), Brian Kowalski (Vice President, Operations), Sandra Firth (Vice President, Business Development), and David Alarcon (Chief Safety Officer).
**Section 4.15 Environmental Matters**

**(a)** *Compliance.* The Company is, and during the past five (5) years has been, in compliance in all material respects with all Environmental Laws applicable to its business, operations, properties, and assets.

**(b)** *Environmental Permits.* The Company holds all Environmental Permits necessary for the conduct of its business as currently conducted, and all such Environmental Permits are in full force and effect. Schedule 4.15(b) sets forth a true and complete list of all twenty-three (23) active Environmental Permits held by the Company, including a description of each permit, the issuing Governmental Authority, the permit number, and the expiration date. The Company is in compliance in all material respects with the terms and conditions of all Environmental Permits. No Action is pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened to revoke, suspend, cancel, terminate, modify, or not renew any Environmental Permit.

**(c)** *No Releases.* Except as disclosed on Schedule 4.15(c), there has been no Release of any Hazardous Substance at, on, under, or from any property currently or formerly owned, operated, or leased by the Company, or at any location to which the Company has transported, arranged for the transportation of, or arranged for the disposal or treatment of, any Hazardous Substance, in each case that would reasonably be expected to give rise to any material liability of the Company under any Environmental Law.

**(d)** *No Proceedings.* Except as disclosed on Schedule 4.15(d), there are no Actions pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened against the Company under any Environmental Law, including any claims, orders, directives, or notices of potential responsibility relating to any Release or threatened Release of any Hazardous Substance, or any claim for investigation, cleanup, removal, remediation, response, corrective action, natural resource damages, property damage, personal injury, or fines or penalties under any Environmental Law.

**(e)** *Environmental Reports.* Seller has made available to Buyer copies of all material environmental assessments, audits, studies, reports, analyses, and investigations in the Company\'s possession or control relating to (i) the environmental condition of any property currently or formerly owned, operated, or leased by the Company, or (ii) the Company\'s compliance with Environmental Laws.

**(f)** *Insurance.* The Company maintains environmental impairment liability insurance with Northshore Specialty Insurance Co. with an aggregate policy limit of \$15,000,000 and a per-occurrence limit of \$5,000,000. **(a)** The Company is a party to four (4) active government contracts, each of which is listed on Schedule 4.16, with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, the Washington Department of Ecology, the United States Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management (collectively, the \"Government Contracts\").

**(b)** Each Government Contract is in full force and effect and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, of the applicable Governmental Authority. **(a)** *Pre-Closing Tax Returns.* Seller shall prepare and timely file (or cause to be prepared and timely filed) all Tax Returns of the Company for any Pre-Closing Tax Period that are due (taking into account any valid extensions) after the Closing Date. All such Tax Returns shall be prepared in a manner consistent with past practice (unless otherwise required by applicable Law). **(b)** *Non-Solicitation.* For a period of three (3) years following the Closing Date, Seller shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to, directly or indirectly, (i) solicit, recruit, hire, or engage (or attempt to solicit, recruit, hire, or engage) any employee of the Company, or (ii) solicit or encourage (or attempt to solicit or encourage) any customer, supplier, licensee, licensor, or other business relationship of the Company to cease or reduce its business with the Company; *provided* that the foregoing shall not restrict (A) general solicitations of employment not specifically directed toward employees of the Company, including through advertisements in newspapers, trade journals, or online job boards, or (B) solicitations by headhunters or recruiting firms not specifically directed by Seller or its Affiliates to target employees of the Company.

**(c)** *Remedies.* The Parties acknowledge and agree that a breach of any of the restrictive covenants set forth in this Section 6.09 would cause irreparable damage to Buyer and the Company and that monetary damages alone would not provide an adequate remedy. Accordingly, in the event of any actual or threatened breach by Seller or any of its Affiliates of the provisions of this Section 6.09, Buyer and the Company shall be entitled to seek specific performance and injunctive relief (temporary, preliminary, and permanent) from any court of competent jurisdiction, without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. The restrictive covenants contained in this Section 6.09 are independent of any other provision of this Agreement, and the existence of any claim or cause of action of Seller against Buyer, whether predicated on this Agreement or otherwise, shall not constitute a defense to the enforcement of such restrictive covenants.

**(a)** No Governmental Authority shall have enacted, issued, promulgated, enforced, or entered any Law, order, injunction, judgment, decree, ruling, or other legally binding action (whether temporary, preliminary, or permanent) that is then in effect and that has the effect of making the transactions contemplated by this Agreement illegal or otherwise preventing or prohibiting the consummation of such transactions.
**(b)** The applicable waiting period (and any extension thereof) under the HSR Act in respect of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall have expired or been terminated.

**(c)** No Action by any Governmental Authority shall be pending that seeks to (i) restrain, enjoin, prevent, prohibit, or make illegal the consummation of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (ii) impose limitations on the ability of Buyer to effectively exercise full rights of ownership of the Shares, or (iii) compel Buyer or any of its Affiliates to dispose of or hold separate all or a material portion of the business or assets of the Company.
**Section 7.02 Conditions to Buyer\'s Obligations**

The obligations of Buyer to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall be subject to the satisfaction (or waiver by Buyer) at or prior to the Closing of the following conditions:

**(a)** *Representations and Warranties.* (i) The Fundamental Representations of Seller shall be true and correct in all respects (other than de minimis inaccuracies) as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date, in which case such representation or warranty shall be true and correct as of such earlier date); and (ii) each other representation and warranty of Seller and the Company contained in this Agreement (without giving effect to any qualification as to \"materiality\" or \"Material Adverse Effect\" contained therein) shall be true and correct as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Closing Date as though made on and as of such date (except to the extent that any such representation or warranty expressly relates to an earlier date), except, in the case of this clause (ii), where the failure of such representations and warranties to be true and correct would not, individually or in the aggregate, reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect.

**(b)** *Covenants.* Seller shall have performed and complied in all material respects with all covenants and agreements required to be performed or complied with by Seller under this Agreement at or prior to the Closing.

**[Section 2: Material Adverse Effect Definition]{.underline}**
**[2.1 Firm Standard on MAE Definitions]{.underline}**

The Material Adverse Effect (\"MAE\") definition is one of the most heavily negotiated provisions in any acquisition agreement and is critical to the buyer\'s closing conditions and representation structure. The MAE definition determines whether an adverse development at the target between signing and closing constitutes a material adverse change that would permit the buyer to decline to close, and it also qualifies many of the seller\'s representations and warranties (e.g., \"no events have occurred that have had or would reasonably be expected to have a Material Adverse Effect\"). Because of the MAE definition\'s outsized impact on the buyer\'s rights, associates must review it with extreme care.

The MAE definition should be narrowly tailored to capture genuine, target-specific material adverse changes in the business, operations, financial condition, assets, liabilities, or results of operations of the target company. The definition should be broad enough to encompass any type of material adverse development, without limiting the concept to a particular category of harm.

**Standard Carve-outs.** It is market practice for the MAE definition to include carve-outs (exclusions) for certain categories of changes or events that are beyond the target\'s control and that affect the broader economy or markets rather than the target specifically. The following carve-outs are generally acceptable:

**THIS IS A CRITICAL REQUIREMENT.** All industry-specific carve-outs and regulatory carve-outs in the MAE definition MUST include a \"disproportionate impact\" exception. This is a firm-wide requirement and is non-negotiable for environmental services transactions. The standard formulation the firm requires is:

**Rationale.** Without the disproportionate impact qualifier, industry-specific and regulatory carve-outs can effectively hollow out the MAE definition, rendering it meaningless. This risk is especially acute for environmental services companies. Consider the following scenario: if the MAE definition carves out \"changes in environmental laws or regulations\" or \"changes affecting the environmental services industry generally\" without a disproportionate impact qualifier, the seller could argue that virtually any adverse regulatory development --- including a new CERCLA regulation that specifically targets the target\'s disposal practices, a state-level ban on a waste treatment methodology that constitutes 40% of the target\'s revenue, or an EPA enforcement initiative directed at the specific category of environmental services the target provides --- is excluded from the MAE definition because it \"affects the environmental services industry generally\" or constitutes a \"change in environmental law.\" This interpretation would render the buyer\'s closing condition (no MAE since signing) essentially unenforceable, because the most likely sources of material adverse change for an environmental services company are precisely the regulatory and industry changes that the carve-out would exclude.

The disproportionate impact qualifier resolves this problem by providing that even if a change is of the type described in the carve-out (e.g., a general change in environmental law), it still counts toward the MAE analysis to the extent it disproportionately affects the target compared to other industry participants. This preserves the buyer\'s protection against target-specific harm while still excluding truly general, industry-wide developments that affect all participants equally.

**Specific Instruction.** If the seller\'s draft excludes \"changes in the environmental services industry generally\" or \"changes in environmental laws or regulations\" from the MAE definition without a disproportionate impact qualifier, this MUST be flagged and corrected. The associate should add the disproportionate impact qualifier language set forth above. **Priority: CRITICAL.**

**[2.2 Environmental-Sector-Specific MAE Considerations]{.underline}**

Beyond the general requirement for the disproportionate impact qualifier addressed in Section 2.1, associates must be attentive to several additional MAE issues that are unique to environmental services acquisitions.

**Regulatory Exposure.** Environmental services companies are uniquely exposed to regulatory changes that could devastate the target\'s value. Changes in CERCLA regulations, modifications to RCRA permitting requirements, new EPA enforcement policies, state-level environmental law changes, and shifts in regulatory interpretation can fundamentally alter the target\'s business model, cost structure, and liability exposure. A broadly worded regulatory carve-out without a disproportionate impact qualifier would allow the seller to argue that sweeping regulatory changes affecting the target --- even those directed specifically at the target\'s business practices --- are excluded from the MAE definition. This is precisely the scenario the disproportionate impact qualifier is designed to address, and its importance in the environmental services context cannot be overstated.

**Pending or Threatened Litigation.** Associates should carefully review whether the MAE definition carves out \"changes resulting from pending or threatened litigation.\" In many general middle-market transactions, this carve-out is unremarkable. However, for environmental services targets with known environmental exposure --- including targets that are potentially responsible parties (\"PRPs\") at CERCLA Superfund sites, targets with ongoing state environmental enforcement actions, or targets facing private contribution or cost-recovery claims --- a litigation carve-out could exclude from the MAE definition precisely the type of adverse development most likely to occur. If the target has known environmental litigation exposure, the associate should either (a) remove the litigation carve-out entirely, or (b) add an express exclusion to the litigation carve-out providing that it does not apply to environmental litigation or claims arising under CERCLA, RCRA, or state environmental law equivalents.

**CERCLA Exposure.** Specifically, exposures of the type associated with CERCLA response cost liability --- such as EPA information requests under CERCLA Section 104(e), PRP notification letters, unilateral administrative orders, and contributions to Superfund remediation costs --- should not be carved out of the MAE definition. These \"Dalton Creek-type\" CERCLA exposures (referring to the category of historical disposal site liabilities frequently encountered in environmental services due diligence) represent some of the most significant and unpredictable risks to environmental services companies, and the buyer must retain the ability to invoke the MAE closing condition if such liabilities materialize or escalate between signing and closing.

**Associates should confirm** that the MAE definition, read as a whole, does not inadvertently exclude from the MAE analysis the categories of adverse developments most relevant to the environmental services target being acquired. If in doubt, escalate to the responsible partner.

**[Section 4: Representations and Warranties --- Survival Periods]{.underline}**
**[4.1 General Survival Framework]{.underline}**

**General Representations.** All other representations and warranties (other than Fundamental Representations, Tax Representations, and Environmental Representations, which are addressed in Section 4.2 below) should survive for a period of eighteen (18) to twenty-four (24) months post-closing. The market range for general representation survival in middle-market PE transactions is fifteen (15) to twenty-four (24) months. A survival period within this range is acceptable. A survival period below fifteen (15) months should be pushed back, as it provides the buyer with insufficient time to discover breaches, particularly breaches that may not become apparent until the buyer has operated the business through a full annual cycle. The firm\'s preferred position is twenty-four (24) months.

**Independence of Basket and Survival.** Associates should note that the basket (deductible) structure is independent of the survival period. Claims must be asserted during the applicable survival period (i.e., the buyer must provide written notice of a claim before the survival period expires), but the basket is a separate limitation on recovery that operates independently. A claim timely asserted during the survival period is not extinguished merely because the aggregate basket threshold has not yet been met; rather, timely-asserted claims accumulate and become recoverable once the basket threshold is satisfied.
**[4.2 Environmental Representations --- Extended Survival]{.underline}**

**THIS IS A CRITICAL REQUIREMENT.** For targets in the environmental services sector, environmental representations --- including but not limited to representations regarding environmental compliance, Environmental Permits, hazardous materials and hazardous waste management, CERCLA and Superfund matters, environmental remediation obligations, environmental insurance, and environmental litigation --- MUST survive for a minimum of thirty-six (36) months post-closing. The firm\'s preferred position is survival for the full applicable statute of limitations (which, for CERCLA claims, is effectively indefinite, as CERCLA imposes strict, joint and several liability with no statute of repose in many circumstances).

**Coordination with Special Indemnity.** The environmental representation survival period is separate from and in addition to the Special Indemnity for known environmental liabilities (see Section 6 below). The Special Indemnity addresses specifically identified environmental matters with a separate seventy-two (72) month survival period. The environmental representation survival period addresses breaches of the environmental representations generally --- i.e., undisclosed environmental liabilities and inaccuracies in the environmental representations that are not covered by the Special Indemnity.
**[Section 5: Indemnification Structure]{.underline}**
**[5.1 Indemnification Cap]{.underline}**

**R&W Insurance Considerations.** In transactions where the buyer is obtaining representations and warranties insurance (see Section 8), the indemnification cap may be subject to additional negotiation dynamics. The R&W insurer may require a certain retention level (the amount of loss the buyer must bear before the policy responds), which interacts with the SPA\'s basket/deductible and cap structure. However, the SPA cap itself must conform to the term sheet regardless of the R&W Insurance structure. The R&W Insurance policy supplements the seller\'s indemnification obligations --- it does not replace them, and the availability of insurance does not justify a reduction in the SPA cap below the term sheet level.
**[5.2 Basket / Deductible]{.underline}**
**[5.3 Sandbagging]{.underline}**
**[5.4 Escrow Mechanics]{.underline}**

> \(b\) **Fundamental Representations and Special Indemnity Escrow.** Released thirty-six (36) months post-closing, less any amounts reserved for pending and unresolved claims as of the release date. This extended hold period corresponds to the minimum environmental representation survival period and the extended escrow for Special Indemnity claims.
**[Section 6: Special Indemnities for Known Environmental Liabilities]{.underline}**

**THIS IS A CRITICAL REQUIREMENT.** Where due diligence has identified a specific, known environmental liability --- such as a pending or threatened CERCLA claim, an EPA information request under CERCLA Section 104(e), a state environmental enforcement action, an ongoing remediation obligation, or any other identified environmental matter --- and the estimated potential liability is \$1,000,000 or more, the SPA MUST include a \"Special Indemnity\" provision for that specific liability.
The Special Indemnity is a distinct indemnification mechanism that operates separately from and in addition to the general representation and warranty indemnification. Its parameters are as follows:

**Survival.** The Special Indemnity must survive for seventy-two (72) months (six years) post-closing. This extended survival period reflects the long-tail nature of CERCLA and environmental enforcement actions, which --- as discussed in Section 4.2 --- often take years to progress from initial inquiry to resolution. A seventy-two month survival period provides the buyer with a meaningful window within which to assert claims as the environmental matter develops and the buyer\'s actual losses become ascertainable.

**Not Subject to the Basket/Deductible.** The Special Indemnity is a dollar-one indemnification obligation. It is not subject to the general deductible described in Section 5.2. The rationale is straightforward: the basket/deductible is designed to filter out immaterial or de minimis claims arising from general representation breaches. A known environmental liability with an estimated exposure of \$1,000,000 or more is, by definition, not immaterial --- it is a specifically identified risk that has been factored into the purchase price negotiation and that requires dedicated indemnification protection.

**Not Subject to the General Cap.** The Special Indemnity is not counted toward the general indemnification cap described in Section 5.1. It operates as a separate, independent indemnification obligation with its own limitations. The Special Indemnity may be subject to its own sub-cap, which is negotiated on a matter-specific basis and typically reflects the high end of the estimated liability range identified in the environmental due diligence. For example, if the estimated liability range for a CERCLA exposure is \$1,500,000 to \$6,000,000, the Special Indemnity sub-cap might be negotiated at \$6,000,000 or \$7,500,000 (the high end of the range plus a reasonable buffer).

**Escrow.** Escrow funds designated for the Special Indemnity should be held for thirty-six (36) months post-closing, consistent with the extended escrow for Fundamental Representations described in Section 5.4. After thirty-six months, the buyer may still assert Special Indemnity claims (through the seventy-two month survival period), but recovery would be sought directly from the seller rather than from escrow.

**Specific Identification.** The Special Indemnity provision must specifically identify the environmental matter by name, site location, applicable regulatory proceeding number (if any), nature of the liability (e.g., \"CERCLA response cost liability arising from historical disposal at \[Site Name\]\"), and the specific representation or due diligence finding that identified the matter. The identified matters should be listed on a dedicated schedule to the SPA (typically a \"Schedule of Scheduled Environmental Matters\" or similar title).

**Specific Instruction.** If environmental due diligence has identified a known CERCLA exposure --- such as a pending EPA information request at a specific disposal facility --- with an estimated liability range of \$1,500,000 to \$6,000,000, the associate MUST ensure that the SPA contains a Special Indemnity provision specifically covering that exposure. If the seller\'s draft SPA fails to include such a provision, the associate should draft and insert a Special Indemnity provision and raise it with the seller\'s counsel as a required addition. Do not treat the absence of a Special Indemnity as a minor markup item; it is a **Critical** priority item that must be escalated to the responsible partner if the seller resists.
**Sample Special Indemnity Language:**

> *\"(c) The Special Environmental Indemnity shall not be subject to the Deductible set forth in Section \[\_\_\] or the Cap set forth in Section \[\_\_\]. The maximum aggregate liability of Seller under this Section \[\_\_\] with respect to each Scheduled Environmental Matter shall be the amount set forth opposite such Scheduled Environmental Matter on Schedule 6.1 (each, a \'Special Indemnity Sub-Cap\').*

**[Section 8: Representations and Warranties Insurance (R&W Insurance)]{.underline}**
**[8.1 When R&W Insurance Is Used]{.underline}**

Representations and warranties insurance (\"R&W Insurance\") is increasingly standard in PE acquisitions in the environmental services sector, particularly for transactions with enterprise values above \$100 million. The buyer typically procures a buy-side R&W Insurance policy to supplement (not replace) the seller\'s direct indemnification obligations under the SPA. The buy-side policy provides the buyer with a direct claim against the insurer for losses arising from breaches of the seller\'s representations and warranties, subject to the policy\'s terms, conditions, exclusions, retentions, and limits.

Common providers of R&W Insurance in recent environmental services transactions handled by the firm include Granite Ridge Underwriters and similar specialty insurers with experience in the environmental sector. The premium for a buy-side policy is typically 2.5% to 4.0% of the policy limit, paid by the buyer at closing. The policy limit is typically set at the general indemnification cap under the SPA.

**Key Policy Exclusions.** R&W Insurance policies in environmental services transactions typically include exclusions for: (a) known matters (i.e., matters specifically identified in the due diligence process or disclosed on the seller\'s disclosure schedules); (b) environmental liabilities (or, in some cases, sub-limits for environmental liabilities rather than a complete exclusion); (c) specific pre-identified risks flagged by the insurer during underwriting; and (d) forward-looking statements and projections.

These exclusions underscore the critical importance of the Special Indemnity provisions described in Section 6. Because the R&W Insurance policy will typically exclude or sub-limit coverage for known environmental liabilities, the seller\'s direct indemnification through the Special Indemnity is the buyer\'s primary source of protection for specifically identified environmental exposures. The R&W Insurance policy and the Special Indemnity serve complementary but distinct functions, and both must be in place.
**[8.2 Subrogation Waiver Requirement]{.underline}**

**THIS IS A HIGH-PRIORITY REQUIREMENT.** Where the buyer is obtaining R&W Insurance, the SPA MUST include a provision waiving the R&W insurer\'s subrogation rights against the seller, except in cases of seller fraud.

**Standard Formulation.** The SPA should provide that the buyer shall cause the R&W Insurance policy to include a provision waiving the insurer\'s right of subrogation against the seller and its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, and representatives, except to the extent any losses arise from or relate to fraud committed by the seller. The waiver should run to the benefit of the seller and its related parties and should be irrevocable for the term of the policy.

**Rationale.** The subrogation waiver is a key commercial term in any R&W Insurance-backed transaction. Without the waiver, the R&W insurer --- after paying a claim to the buyer --- could \"step into the buyer\'s shoes\" and pursue subrogation claims against the seller to recover the amounts paid. This subrogation right would effectively nullify the benefit of R&W Insurance from the seller\'s perspective, because the seller would face the same indemnification exposure (now from the insurer rather than the buyer) that the insurance was supposed to address. The subrogation waiver eliminates this circular liability and is a standard market practice that sellers commonly require as a condition to agreeing to the overall indemnification structure, including the cap, basket, and escrow terms.

The exception for fraud preserves the insurer\'s (and the buyer\'s) rights against a seller who has committed fraud in connection with the transaction. A fraudulent seller is not entitled to the benefit of the subrogation waiver, and the insurer should retain full recourse against such a seller.

**Specific Instruction.** If the seller\'s draft SPA makes no reference to R&W Insurance or to the waiver of insurer subrogation rights, the associate must add an R&W Insurance subrogation waiver provision. In many transactions, the availability and structure of R&W Insurance is negotiated at the term-sheet level, and the subrogation waiver is a term-sheet-level commitment. Its omission from the SPA must be corrected. **Priority: HIGH.**

> *\"Buyer shall obtain and maintain a representations and warranties insurance policy (the \'R&W Insurance Policy\') and shall cause such R&W Insurance Policy to provide that the insurer thereunder shall waive, and shall not exercise or pursue, any right of subrogation or any other right of recovery against Seller or any of its Affiliates, directors, officers, employees, agents, or representatives with respect to any claim made by Buyer under such R&W Insurance Policy, except to the extent such claim arises from or relates to Fraud by Seller. Buyer shall not amend, modify, or waive any provision of the R&W Insurance Policy in a manner that would adversely affect Seller\'s rights under this Section \[\_\_\] without Seller\'s prior written consent.\"*

**Coordination with Other Provisions.** The availability of R&W Insurance does not change the SPA\'s indemnification cap, escrow requirements, or other indemnification terms. The R&W Insurance policy is a supplement to the seller\'s direct indemnification obligations, not a substitute for them. Associates should resist any seller argument that the availability of R&W Insurance justifies a lower SPA indemnification cap or a smaller escrow.

## SPA MARKUP MEMORANDUM

**Project Cascade — Acquisition of Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.**  
**Buyer:** Whitmore Capital Partners LLC  
**Seller:** Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.  
**Target:** Cascadia Environmental Solutions, Inc.  
**Date:** October 29, 2025  
**To:** Elena Vasquez-Moreno, Partner, M&A Practice Group  
**From:** Jonathan Kreider, Senior Associate, M&A Practice Group  
**Re:** Buyer-side review of Seller’s Stock Purchase Agreement draft

---

## Executive Summary

The Seller’s draft is materially seller-favorable and requires a focused buyer markup. The draft departs from the executed September 10, 2025 term sheet on the general indemnification cap, omits the agreed Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, and uses an anti-sandbagging clause and an affirmative earnout operating covenant that are inconsistent with the buyer playbook. It also does not address the federal and state government-contract novation/recognition process or change-of-control environmental-permit notifications with the specificity warranted by the diligence findings.

The following positions should be treated as the buyer’s principal markup instructions:

| Priority | SPA provision | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| Critical | Article I — MAE | Add a disproportionate-impact exception to both the environmental-services-industry and Environmental Laws carve-outs. |
| Critical | Section 2.05(d) — Earnout operations | Delete the past-practice/maximize covenant and replace it with the narrow primary-purpose negative covenant. |
| Critical | Article VII / Section 6.12 — Government contracts | Add specific FAR Part 42.12 and state novation/recognition covenants, representations, and a tailored closing condition. |
| Critical | Article IX / new Section 9.09 — Dalton Creek | Add a 72-month Special Indemnity, dollar-one, outside the general basket and cap, with a 36-month escrow holdback. |
| Critical | Section 9.06 — Sandbagging | Delete the anti-sandbagging provision and replace it with express pro-sandbagging language. |
| High | Sections 1.01 and 9.04(b) — General cap | Replace $43,000,000 / 20% with $26,875,000 / 12.5%, as required by the binding term sheet. |
| High | Section 9.01 — Environmental survival | Carve environmental representations out of the 12-month general period and provide at least 36 months; reserve the right to seek the applicable limitations period. |
| High | Section 6.01 — Affiliate transactions | Add a consent restriction covering entering into, amending, extending, renewing, or terminating Seller/Affiliate transactions. |
| High | Sections 2.03(d), 2.08, 7.02 — Debt payoff | Require executed payoff letters at least three business days before Closing and simultaneous payoff through the funds flow as a closing condition. |
| Medium | Section 6.13 — Environmental permits | Add pre-closing notification/approval and post-closing cooperation covenants covering the 23 permits in Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada. |
| Medium | Section 10.13 / Section 7.02 — R&W insurance | Add a fraud-only subrogation waiver and a closing deliverable confirming the policy is bound and effective. |
| Medium | Section 6.09 — Restrictive covenants | Conform duration, geography, business scope, and carve-outs to the term sheet; remove the five-year nationwide “any business” prohibition. |

### Immediate escalation items

1. Confirm with the client whether government-contract novation/recognition must be a hard closing condition or whether submission/no-denial plus a post-closing cooperation covenant is the acceptable compromise. The recommended markup uses the latter as the operative condition, with a right to require completion where a contracting officer requires it.
2. Confirm whether the client wants to move from the 36-month environmental-representation survival compromise to the full applicable limitations period. The markup below uses 36 months as the minimum and preserves the buyer’s full-limitations-period ask in the comment.
3. Confirm the county and date of the Dalton Creek EPA Section 104(e) request. The DD memo identifies Clackamas County and a February 12, 2025 request, while the Seller’s Schedule 4.15(d) identifies Lane County and June 12, 2025. The Special Indemnity schedule must be conformed to the underlying EPA letter before circulation.

---

## Materials Reviewed and Drafting Conventions

This memorandum cross-references: (i) the executed Binding Term Sheet dated September 10, 2025; (ii) the Buyer’s M&A Playbook for Environmental Services Sector Acquisitions, Version 4.2; (iii) the Environmental Due Diligence Summary dated October 18, 2025; (iv) the Seller’s draft SPA circulated October 22, 2025; and (v) the October 23, 2025 partner instructions.

Each issue below includes the Seller’s draft language, complete buyer-ready replacement or insertion language, a track-changes-style comment, and a priority. Section references are to the Seller’s draft unless otherwise indicated. Defined terms used below have the meanings in the SPA unless revised below.

---

# I. ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS

## 1. Material Adverse Effect — disproportionate-impact qualifiers

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller’s draft language

> “Material Adverse Effect” means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); (v) acts of war, epidemics, pandemics, natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) announcement or pendency of the transactions; (vii) actions taken at Buyer’s request or consent; or (viii) failure to meet projections, subject to the underlying facts being considered.

### Buyer’s proposed replacement

> **“Material Adverse Effect”** means any event, change, effect, development, state of facts, condition, circumstance, or occurrence that, individually or in the aggregate, has had or would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect on (a) the business, assets, liabilities, financial condition, or results of operations of the Company, or (b) the ability of Seller to consummate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; provided, however, that none of the following, individually or in the aggregate, shall be deemed to constitute, or shall be taken into account in determining whether there has been or would reasonably be expected to be, a Material Adverse Effect: (i) changes in general economic, financial, credit, securities market, or political conditions in the United States or globally; (ii) changes in conditions generally affecting the environmental services industry, **except to the extent such changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the environmental services industry**; (iii) changes in Environmental Laws or regulations, **except to the extent such changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other participants in the environmental services industry**; (iv) changes in GAAP or applicable Law (other than Environmental Laws, which are addressed in clause (iii) above); (v) acts of war, whether or not declared, armed hostilities, sabotage, terrorism, military actions, or any escalation or worsening thereof, epidemics, pandemics, earthquakes, hurricanes, tornadoes, floods, or other natural disasters or acts of God; (vi) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including any impact on relationships with customers, suppliers, employees, or Governmental Authorities; (vii) any action taken by the Company at the express written request or with the express written consent of Buyer; and (viii) any failure by the Company to meet any internal or external projections, forecasts, or estimates of revenue, earnings, or other financial performance metrics for any period, provided that the underlying facts, circumstances, and causes of any such failure may be considered in determining whether a Material Adverse Effect has occurred.

### Comment / rationale

The draft’s unqualified carve-outs remove from the MAE analysis the two categories most likely to affect this environmental-services target: industry economics and environmental regulation. Add the disproportionate-impact qualifier to both carve-outs. No other change to the MAE definition is necessary at this stage. **Sources:** Term Sheet § 12 (Buyer closing condition); Playbook §§ 2.1–2.2 and 14, item 1; Partner Instructions ¶¶ 52–67; DD Memo §§ V–VI.

## 2. Adjusted EBITDA definition and earnout calculation methodology

**Priority: Medium**

### Seller’s draft language

> “Adjusted EBITDA” means, with respect to any period, the net income of the Company for such period, determined in accordance with GAAP applied consistently with the Company’s past practice, plus (a) interest expense, (b) income tax expense, and (c) depreciation and amortization expense, in each case to the extent deducted in computing net income, and further adjusted to exclude (i) non-recurring transaction costs incurred in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, (ii) purchase-price accounting adjustments arising from the consummation of the transactions, (iii) extraordinary or non-recurring items, and (iv) management fees, monitoring fees, or similar fees charged by Buyer or any of its Affiliates to the Company, in each case as determined in accordance with GAAP applied consistently with the Company’s past practice. The detailed calculation methodology for Adjusted EBITDA is set forth on Exhibit D.

### Buyer’s proposed replacement

> **“Adjusted EBITDA”** means, with respect to the Measurement Period, the net income of the Company for such period, determined in accordance with GAAP applied consistently with the Company’s past practice, plus (a) interest expense, (b) income tax expense, and (c) depreciation and amortization expense, in each case to the extent deducted in computing net income, and further adjusted to exclude or add back, without duplication: (i) reasonable and documented transaction expenses incurred in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement; (ii) purchase-price accounting adjustments arising from the consummation of the transactions; (iii) Buyer-directed integration costs, restructuring charges, and other costs incurred at the direction of Buyer or any Affiliate of Buyer in connection with integrating, consolidating, or reorganizing the Company; (iv) extraordinary, unusual, or non-recurring items, including one-time litigation costs, regulatory penalties, and other extraordinary items; (v) corporate overhead allocations, management fees, monitoring fees, or similar charges imposed by Buyer or any Affiliate of Buyer that were not charged to the Company on a substantially consistent basis before the Closing; (vi) intercompany charges imposed by Buyer or any Affiliate of Buyer that are not for goods or services provided to the Company at fair market value and on terms no less favorable to the Company than those available from an unaffiliated third party; and (vii) expenses attributable to the Affiliate Lease or any other transaction with Seller or an Affiliate of Seller to the extent such expenses exceed fair market value or the amount that would have been incurred in an arm’s-length transaction. Adjusted EBITDA shall not include any add-back, exclusion, or adjustment that would result in double counting, and shall not be reduced by any costs or charges allocated to the Company solely as a result of Buyer’s post-Closing accounting policies or integration decisions, except to the extent expressly included in an adjustment described above. The calculation shall be made using the same accounting principles, classifications, and methodologies used in the Company’s historical financial statements, except as expressly provided in this definition. The detailed calculation methodology set forth on Exhibit D shall be conformed to this definition.

### Comment / rationale

The term sheet requires the $25,000,000 maximum, $38,000,000 full-payment threshold, $32,000,000 floor, linear interpolation, and December 31, 2026 Measurement Period; the numerical mechanics in Sections 2.05(a)–(b) generally conform. The draft definition, however, should expressly address Buyer-directed integration/restructuring costs and non-recurring/intercompany allocations so that Buyer can implement the platform strategy without creating avoidable earnout disputes. The existing Exhibit D should be replaced with a detailed schedule consistent with this definition. **Sources:** Term Sheet §§ 5 and 13; Playbook §§ 7.1–7.2; Partner Instructions ¶¶ 107–111; DD Memo § VIII.

---

# II. ARTICLE II — PURCHASE PRICE, EARNOUT, AND CLOSING DELIVERABLES

## 3. Section 2.05(d) — earnout operating covenant

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller’s draft language

> From and after the Closing Date through the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall, and shall cause the Company to, operate the business of the Company in a manner consistent with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment. Without limiting the foregoing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action that would reasonably be expected to reduce the Adjusted EBITDA of the Company below the levels that would otherwise have been achieved. In furtherance of the foregoing, during the Earnout Period, Buyer shall cause the Company to maintain substantially the same level of personnel, equipment, and other resources as in effect immediately prior to the Closing Date and shall not divert or redirect any contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities of the Company to Buyer or any of its Affiliates.

### Buyer’s proposed replacement

> **(d) Operation of the Business During the Earnout Period.** Following the Closing, Buyer shall not, and shall cause the Company not to, take any action with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this Section 2.05(d) shall restrict Buyer’s right to operate, integrate, restructure, consolidate, or otherwise manage the Company and its business in Buyer’s sole discretion, including the right to make capital expenditure decisions, change pricing or compensation strategies, make personnel decisions, enter new markets, make strategic investments, acquire or dispose of businesses or assets, allocate corporate overhead, combine or separate operations, and make other operational modifications. Buyer shall have no obligation to operate the Company in a manner consistent with past practice, maximize the Earnout Payment, maintain the Company as a separate entity, maintain any particular level of personnel, equipment, capital expenditures, or other resources, retain any particular employee, or refrain from diverting or redirecting contracts, customers, revenues, or business opportunities, and no such action shall constitute a breach of this Section 2.05(d) unless taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the Earnout Payment.

### Comment / rationale

Delete the affirmative past-practice, maximize, resource-maintenance, and anti-diversion obligations. They would restrict Buyer’s platform integration and restructuring plans and create litigation over ordinary business decisions. The replacement preserves a narrow protection against bad-faith manipulation while maintaining Buyer’s operational flexibility. **Sources:** Term Sheet § 5 (agreed primary-purpose covenant); Playbook § 7.2 and checklist item 7; Partner Instructions ¶¶ 88–105.

## 4. Section 2.05(c) and (e) — earnout timing mechanics

**Priority: Medium**

### Seller’s draft language

> Within sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller an Earnout Statement. Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable shall be paid within ten (10) Business Days after the final determination of Adjusted EBITDA.

### Buyer’s proposed replacement

> **(c) Earnout Calculation and Dispute Resolution.** Within forty-five (45) days after the end of the Earnout Period, Buyer shall prepare and deliver to Seller a written statement (the “Earnout Statement”) setting forth Buyer’s good-faith calculation of Adjusted EBITDA for the Earnout Period, together with reasonable supporting documentation. Seller shall have thirty (30) days after receipt of the Earnout Statement to review it and deliver a written objection specifying each disputed item and the basis for the objection. The dispute resolution procedures set forth in Section 2.04(b) and Section 2.04(c) shall apply mutatis mutandis to any dispute with respect to the Earnout Statement.
>
> **(e) Payment of Earnout.** Any Earnout Payment determined to be payable shall be paid by Buyer to Seller no later than sixty (60) days after the end of the Earnout Period; provided, however, that if Seller timely delivers an objection and the amount of the Earnout Payment has not been finally determined by that date, Buyer shall pay the finally determined amount within ten (10) Business Days after such final determination. For U.S. federal income tax purposes, the Parties agree to treat any Earnout Payment as an adjustment to the Purchase Price.

### Comment / rationale

The executed term sheet calls for delivery of the calculation within 45 days and payment within 60 days after the Measurement Period. Conform the SPA to those agreed mechanics while preserving a practical payment rule for a timely disputed calculation. **Sources:** Term Sheet § 5; Partner Instructions ¶¶ 107–111.

## 5. Sections 2.03(d), 2.08(a), and 7.02 — closing debt payoff

**Priority: High**

### Seller’s draft language

> **Section 2.03(d):** At or promptly following the Closing, Buyer shall cause the Company to repay, discharge, and satisfy in full all Closing Indebtedness. Seller shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Buyer in connection with the repayment of such Closing Indebtedness.

The Seller’s closing deliverables do not require payoff letters. Section 7.02 contains no separate payoff-letter condition.

### Buyer’s proposed replacement and additions

> **Section 2.03(d) — Repayment of Closing Indebtedness.** Seller shall deliver to Buyer executed payoff letters from each holder of Closing Indebtedness, including Cascade Mutual Bank with respect to the senior term loan, Pacific Lease Corp. with respect to the equipment financing, and Seller with respect to the subordinated seller note, no later than three (3) Business Days before the Closing Date. Each payoff letter shall state the total amount required to repay the applicable Closing Indebtedness in full as of the Closing Date, including principal, accrued interest, prepayment premiums, breakage costs, and all other amounts required to discharge the obligation; provide wire instructions; and provide for the release, upon receipt of the payoff amount, of all liens and other Encumbrances securing such Closing Indebtedness, including delivery of UCC termination statements and other lien-release documents. At the Closing, the applicable payoff amounts shall be paid directly to the applicable holders through the funds flow agreed by the Parties. All Closing Indebtedness shall be fully repaid, discharged, and released simultaneously with the Closing, and no Closing Indebtedness or related Encumbrance shall remain outstanding after the Closing.
>
> **Section 2.08(a)(x) — Payoff Letters and Lien Releases.** Executed payoff letters satisfying Section 2.03(d), together with customary lien-release documents and UCC termination statements (or irrevocable commitments to deliver the same upon receipt of the payoff amounts), from each holder of Closing Indebtedness.
>
> **Section 7.02(h) — Payoff Letters.** Seller shall have delivered the payoff letters and related lien-release documentation required by Section 2.03(d) at least three (3) Business Days before the Closing Date, and the Parties shall have agreed to the final funds flow providing for simultaneous repayment of all Closing Indebtedness at the Closing.

### Comment / rationale

The term sheet makes payoff letters a binding requirement and requires simultaneous payoff through the closing funds flow. “At or promptly following” is inadequate for Buyer and its acquisition lender. **Sources:** Term Sheet § 6 and § 12(d); Playbook § 9.2 and checklist item 9; Partner Instructions ¶¶ 193–205.

---

# III. ARTICLE IV — SELLER/COMPANY REPRESENTATIONS

## 6. Section 4.16 — government contract representations

**Priority: Critical**

### Seller’s draft language

> (a) The Company is a party to four (4) active government contracts, each of which is listed on Schedule 4.16, with the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality, the Washington Department of Ecology, the United States Army Corps of Engineers, and the Bureau of Land Management (collectively, the “Government Contracts”).
>
> (b) Each Government Contract is in full force and effect and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, of the applicable Governmental Authority. The Company is not in material breach or default under any Government Contract, and no event has occurred that, with the giving of notice or the lapse of time, or both, would constitute a material breach or default thereunder.
>
> (c) Neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, or employees is subject to debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, or proposed suspension by any Governmental Authority, or is listed on any excluded parties list maintained by any Governmental Authority.
>
> (d) The Company has complied in all material respects with all applicable procurement Laws, regulations, and requirements in connection with the Government Contracts.

### Buyer’s proposed replacement

> **Section 4.16 — Government Contracts.**
>
> **(a)** The Company is a party to the four (4) active government contracts listed on Schedule 4.16: (i) Oregon Department of Environmental Quality Contract No. DEQ-OR-2022-0847; (ii) Washington Department of Ecology Contract No. WA-ECY-2023-1134; (iii) United States Army Corps of Engineers Contract No. W912DR-21-D-0045; and (iv) Bureau of Land Management Contract No. L23PX-00412 (collectively, the “Government Contracts”). Seller has made available to Buyer complete and correct copies of each Government Contract, including all amendments, modifications, task orders, statements of work, and change orders.
>
> **(b)** Each Government Contract is in full force and effect and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Company and, to the Knowledge of the Company, of the applicable Governmental Authority. The Company is not in material breach or default under any Government Contract, and no event has occurred that, with the giving of notice or lapse of time, or both, would constitute a material breach or default thereunder.
>
> **(c)** No Government Contract is subject to any pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened termination for default or convenience, suspension, non-renewal, material modification, cure notice, show-cause notice, or adverse performance determination. No contracting officer or other Governmental Authority has indicated an intent to terminate, suspend, materially modify, or decline to renew any Government Contract as a result of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement.
>
> **(d)** Neither the Company nor any of its directors, officers, or employees is subject to debarment, suspension, proposed debarment, or proposed suspension by any Governmental Authority, or is listed on any excluded parties list maintained by any Governmental Authority.
>
> **(e)** The Company has complied in all material respects with all applicable procurement Laws, regulations, and requirements in connection with the Government Contracts, including the Anti-Assignment Act, 41 U.S.C. § 6305, to the extent applicable, FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12, and all applicable state procurement requirements.
>
> **(f)** Schedule 4.16 identifies each consent, notification, novation agreement, recognition agreement, change-of-name agreement, or other approval required from a Governmental Authority or contracting officer in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement, including the change in ownership or control of the Company.
>
> **(g)** Except as set forth on Schedule 4.16, no consent, novation, recognition agreement, or other approval required under any Government Contract or applicable Law in connection with the transactions contemplated by this Agreement has been denied, withdrawn, or materially conditioned, and Seller and the Company have timely made all required notifications and submissions.

### Comment / rationale

The four contracts collectively represent a material revenue stream. The draft confirms that the contracts exist but does not address termination risk, required novations, or the Anti-Assignment Act/FAR process. Add specific representations, including no pending termination or debarment action and a complete schedule of required approvals. **Sources:** Playbook §§ 12.2, 13.2; DD Memo §§ VI.A–C and VIII; Partner Instructions ¶¶ 113–137.

## 7. Section 4.15(b) — environmental permits and change-of-control risk

**Priority: Medium**

### Seller’s draft language

> The Company holds all Environmental Permits necessary for the conduct of its business as currently conducted, and all such Environmental Permits are in full force and effect. Schedule 4.15(b) sets forth a true and complete list of all twenty-three (23) active Environmental Permits held by the Company, including a description of each permit, the issuing Governmental Authority, the permit number, and the expiration date. The Company is in compliance in all material respects with the terms and conditions of all Environmental Permits. No Action is pending or, to the Knowledge of the Company, threatened to revoke, suspend, cancel, terminate, modify, or not renew any Environmental Permit.

### Buyer’s proposed replacement

> **(b) Environmental Permits.** The Company holds all twenty-three (23) Environmental Permits required for the conduct of its business as currently conducted.
